steps.say: Rocks are grouped by how they form. Igneous rocks form when hot melted rock cools and hardens. Granite and basalt are igneous.
Sedimentary rocks form when layers of sand, mud or shells are pressed together over a very long time. Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary, and they often contain fossils.
Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure change other rocks. Marble and slate are metamorphic.
A fossil forms when a dead plant or animal is buried quickly in sediment. Soft parts rot away, and the hard parts or an imprint stay in the sedimentary rock.
In the rock cycle, rocks are weathered, laid down, buried, heated, melted and cooled again over millions of years. Soil is broken rock plus the remains of living things.

check.prompt: Which kind of rock forms when melted rock cools and hardens?

options.why: Metamorphic rock is changed by heat and pressure.

hints: It begins with the letter i.
It is formed from hot, melted rock.
check.explanation: Igneous rock forms when melted rock cools and becomes solid.

check.prompt: In which kind of rock are fossils usually found?

options.why: The heat would destroy a fossil.
The heat and pressure would damage fossils.

hints: Fossils form in layers of mud and sand.
